content.text: I read every input file, all ten draft sections, the numeral ledger, and all six figure briefs, and traced each item against the disclosure.

input.summary: Full ledger review completed against input/disclosure.md (sole technical authority; input/conversation.md is a truncated duplicate ending mid-sentence at "retained by", and input/brief.md was used only for formalities: applicant/inventor Nimo Rotem, no priority claim, no federal support — matching draft/02 and draft/03 "Not applicable"). Every limitation of all 17 claims (independent claims 1, 12, 16 and dependents 2-11, 13-15, 17) was traced to affirmative disclosure text: shell/floor/side walls/upper edge, tray suspended on feet with lower return passage, tray side walls spaced inward forming two side supply passages, perforations, rigid spacer frame holding two opposed phase-change cassettes above the tray and below the lid, central inlet opening, two downward guide ducts beside the cassettes, peripheral outlet openings, the closed passive circulation path with no fan/pump/powered air mover, depending indexing rib entering the mating channel and shifting the module to the registered overlap, gasket sealing the upper edge after registration, resilient feet pressed against ledges so the module cannot lift away during transport, shallow condensate channel around the tray, openings at the lower ends of the guide ducts discharging condensate, removable absorbent wick with pull tab accessible when the tray is removed and replaceable without opening a cassette, and the mechanical exposure indicator (stem thermally coupled to one cassette, temperature-responsive latch, spring, latched exposed position, manual reset only after opening, no airflow control). The use sequence in claim 12 and the servicing sequence in claims 16-17 track the disclosure's "For use" paragraph and wick paragraph; the optional status of the wick and indicator in the Variations section matches "The wick and the irreversible mechanical exposure indicator are supported optional features." All 30 numerals (10-86) were checked: each has exactly one meaning, each appears in the description, each appears in at least one figure numeral list, and no figure list contains a numeral absent from draft/numerals.md. Cross-references in the description ("Referring to FIG. 1, FIG. 2, and FIG. 5", etc.) were verified to name at least one view carrying each numeral discussed. The single named section line 2-2 uses the same repeated designation in the FIG. 1 brief (repeated at each end with rear-pointing arrows), the FIG. 2 brief, and draft/07; the four unnumbered detail circles in FIG. 2 (centre, right-hand upper, right-hand lower, left-hand) map one-to-one and in the same order to FIG. 3-6 in both the FIG. 2 brief and draft/07, and the "omitted for clarity" statement for FIG. 6 matches between draft/07 and the FIG. 6 brief. Figure geometry was checked for undisclosed functional-surface substance: the rectangular shell/pan/slab outlines, plain indicator housing outline, coil-spring convention and slab-like cassettes are shape-neutral depiction conventions expressly marked schematic, while the substantive statements that were checked — rib side surfaces facing the channel sides, foot bearing down on a horizontal ledge shelf, outlet opening overlapping the upper end of the side supply passage, condensate opening at the lower end of the duct, duct upper ends opening to the space the inlet air divides into along the cassette faces, spring acting outward, stem passing through the wall to a cassette — each trace to an affirmative disclosure sentence ("mating channel"/"shifts the thermal module into a registered position", "presses resilient feet ... against ledges", "peripheral outlet openings aligned with the side supply passages", "Openings at the lower ends of the guide ducts discharge condensate", "divides along faces of the cassettes", "visible from outside"/"latched exposed position", "thermally coupled to one phase-change cassette"). No taper, angle, runout, depth-of-end, or proportion statement was found. No drafting note, placeholder, open question, or unresolved alternative remains, the abstract is 139 words and consistent with claim 1, and no means-plus-function language appears. One internal drawing inconsistency was found and is reported: the FIG. 2 brief omits three features that its own detail circles enlarge in FIG. 3, FIG. 4, and FIG. 5. Prior-art characterizations in the Background were not assessed for inventor support, per instruction.

findings.title: FIG. 2 brief omits the indexing rib and mating channel, the ledge and resilient foot, and the wick that its own detail circles enlarge in FIG. 3, FIG. 4, and FIG. 5
findings.where: figures/FIG-2.md (items "Insulated lid 60", "Removable thermal module 40", "Shell side wall 14", "Shell floor 12") versus figures/FIG-3.md, figures/FIG-4.md, figures/FIG-5.md and draft/07-drawings.md
findings.detail: FIG. 2 is the closed-condition parent view, and its four broken circles are the sole source of the enlarged regions of FIG. 3 through FIG. 6. The FIG. 2 brief does include, unnumbered, the gasket band, the condensate troughs, and the exposure indicator, but it never mentions the depending indexing rib or the mating channel in the region marked by the central circle, never mentions the ledge or the resilient foot in the region marked by the right-hand upper circle, and never mentions the absorbent wick in the trough marked by the right-hand lower circle. Rendered literally from these briefs, FIG. 2 would show a featureless lid underside, a plain unstepped inner face on the shell side wall, and an empty trough, while FIG. 3, FIG. 4, and FIG. 5 enlarge those exact regions and show the rib engaged in the channel, the foot bearing on the ledge, and the wick lying in the trough. A detail view cannot show structure that its parent view lacks at the circled region. All three features are affirmatively disclosed ("the rib enters a mating channel in the spacer frame", "presses resilient feet of the spacer frame against ledges of the shell", "A removable absorbent wick lies in a shallow condensate channel around the product tray"), so the fix adds no unsupported matter and needs no new numerals in FIG. 2.
findings.evidence: FIG-2.md: "Insulated lid 60: a horizontal hatched slab closing the top of the view above the module 40, an unnumbered compressible band lying between its underside and each shell side wall 14." and "Shell side wall 14: two upright hatched slabs, one at each end of the shell floor 12 and joined to it, forming an upwardly open U-shaped section." and "Shell floor 12: ... a shallow upwardly open trough being shown schematically at each side of the tray 20." — no rib, channel, ledge, foot, or wick appears anywhere in the FIG. 2 brief. Against this, FIG-3.md: "Depending indexing rib 62: a downwardly projecting hatched tongue on the underside of the lid 60, shown schematically, aligned above the mating channel 52 and entering it"; FIG-4.md: "Ledge 18: a step on the inward-facing surface of the shell side wall 14 ... Resilient foot 54: a downwardly projecting hatched foot at the outboard lower corner of the frame 42, in contact with and bearing down on the shelf of the ledge 18"; FIG-5.md: "Removable absorbent wick 72: an elongate body lying in the trough of the channel 70". draft/07-drawings.md confirms each detail view is "indicated by" a broken circle "in FIG. 2".
findings.fix: In figures/FIG-2.md, amend three bullets so the parent view carries the enlarged structure, all unnumbered in this view: (1) change the lid bullet to read "Insulated lid 60: a horizontal hatched slab closing the top of the view above the module 40, an unnumbered compressible band lying between its underside and each shell side wall 14, and an unnumbered short tongue depending from its underside at the centre of the width and entering an unnumbered upwardly open recess in the upper surface of the module 40."; (2) change the shell side wall bullet to read "Shell side wall 14: two upright hatched slabs, one at each end of the shell floor 12 and joined to it, forming an upwardly open U-shaped section, an unnumbered step being shown on the inward-facing surface of each slab at the level of the module 40, with an unnumbered short foot depending from the adjacent end of the module 40 onto that step."; (3) change the shell floor bullet to read "Shell floor 12: a horizontal hatched slab spanning the bottom of the view, a shallow upwardly open trough being shown schematically at each side of the tray 20, an unnumbered elongate body lying in each trough." Leave the "Numerals shown on this figure" list for FIG. 2 unchanged.
